review_scope: Independent frozen production source review, whole-TU scalar/immediate-pool ASan+UBSan parity, intended-fault mutants and v81 full-TU compile+assembly. No root edits or phone access.

limits: HMX/HVX/quant use the existing scalar stand-ins
Host does not enable Hexagon-only i24 staging
Only pre-existing scalar exponent shift sanitizer is disabled

fixed_v1_issue: Initial expert==64 guard missed application-compacted active expert arrays. V2 uses 1..64; initial source and codegen archived under v1-dispatch-too-narrow.
device_acceptance_pending: Exact model IDs and normal memory/settings on actual S26.
A diagnostic must show the new leaf selected for all 38 normal all-native LFM prefill calls; warmups separate.
Only balanced normal binaries can establish throughput; no throughput benefit is inferred from scalar packet counts.
limits: Whole-caller HMX, HVX dequant and quant use existing scalar stand-ins. Native TL2 expansion/packing and actual production caller are exercised. DMA and worker jobs execute immediately; submit retains a logical pending token until wait. This checks control/retirement structure, not real concurrency, silicon arithmetic, DMA/cache visibility or timing.
Hexagon-only i24 staging is not enabled in the host fixture; all readout/layout consumers are unchanged by this patch.

The one pre-existing signed-negative exponent shift in swiglu_det.h is suppressed only while compiling standin/hvx_scalar.c (-fno-sanitize=shift-base); both whole kernel TUs and all other sanitizer classes remain enabled.
E60 whole-caller case has two nonempty experts, so it proves compact-count dispatch and sparse expert indexing, not a sixty-active-expert numerical model run.
Whole M1 case omits the M1 GEMV flag and verifies the HMX fallback does not select the new leaf. Actual native decode exits through the existing use_m1 branch before reaching this code.
Gemma fallback is established from immutable geometry guards and unchanged fallback issue sequence, not a new Gemma device benchmark.
No new allocation, buffer, cache, reader, preload, RPC, API/ABI, persistent state or output accumulation order.
